title: Ignatiana: A Research Apparatus for Ignatian Spirituality
description:
A research apparatus for Ignatian spirituality, confined to the old Society (1540–1773) and organised in five lines: the founder's own writings (the Spiritual Exercises in a trilingual public-domain parallel edition — Spanish Autograph, Vulgata of 1548, Mullan 1914 — and the letters of 1524–1547 in full); the school of discernment, carried to its end — the Official Directory of 1599 and Favre's Memoriale (both bilingual), Nadal's In Examen annotationes, Rodríguez's Of Conformity to the Will of God complete, and the Abandonment to Divine Providence attributed to Caussade, carried whole with the attribution stated as debated; the Society in the world (Xavier, and the Imago primi saeculi with its Dutch mirror); Friedrich Spee (Cautio Criminalis and Trutznachtigall); and the counter-voices, from the Monita secreta and Pascal to the brief of 1773 carried complete. With a canonical paragraph-level citation index, a cross-corpus concordance over the whole apparatus, a concept atlas, curated reading paths, a discernment lexicon, registers of persons and places, and a citation-bound dialogue with the corpus.

Four modern translations (Ganss, Padberg, Divarkar, Munitiz) remain in copyright: their structure, statistics and citation anchors are part of the apparatus, but no text of them is distributed — a reader opens them from a copy they own, on their own device.
